title.narrative: Global Child Project of the Global Clean Hydrogen Programme

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The Global Child Project of the GCHP aims to establish the foundational elements necessary for developing clean hydrogen technologies in participa?ting countries by focusing on knowledge management, capacity building, and coordination. These activities will catalyse the transition to clean hydrogen while delivering wide-ranging socio-economic benefits across the programme’s target sectors.The socio-economic benefits of the Global Child Project include:Capacity building and job creation: By fostering capacity-building initiatives such as thematic working groups, e-training sessions, and the creation and management of the Global Knowledge Platform, the Global Child Project will equip stakeholders in participating countries with the technical skills and expertise needed for clean hydrogen production and application. This capacity-building effort will directly contribute to the creation of skilled jobs in sectors linked to hydrogen production, infrastructure development, and technology management. Through the dissemination of knowledge and best practices, the project will support local industries in developing the workforce required to sustain long-term growth in the clean hydrogen economy.Innovation and industrial development: The Global Child Project will promote technological innovation by encouraging collaboration among industry stakeholders, international experts, and governments. By sharing best practices and innovation case studies via the Global Knowledge Platform, the project will help spur the development of hydrogen-related technologies and industries. This will open-up new economic opportunities in industrial and transport sectors and position countries as global frontrunners in the green hydrogen economy. These industries will create direct and indirect jobs, contributing to the broader socio-economic development of participating nations.Energy security and economic resilience: Through its focus on clean hydrogen, the Global Child Project will enhance energy security by supporting the development of locally produced hydrogen as a reliable alternative to imported fossil fuels. This shift will not only reduce dependency on external energy sources but will also stabilise energy prices, making economies more resilient to global energy market fluctuations. Increased energy independence will strengthen national energy systems, enabling countries to better meet their energy demands while ensuring a more sustainable and secure energy future.Gender inclusion and social equity: The Global Child Project will actively promote gender inclusion by ensuring that women and youth are integral participants in all project activities. The project aims for 50% female participation in capacity-building initiatives and a 20% youth participation rate, thereby creating opportunities for underrepresented groups in the clean hydrogen sector. Through focused training programmes and the development of gender-responsive knowledge products, the project will support social equity, providing equal access to new employment opportunities and ensuring that the benefits of the green hydrogen transition are widely shared across communities.Health and environmental benefits: By facilitating the adoption of clean hydrogen technologies, the Global Child Project will help reduce air pollution in industrial and urban areas, contributing to improved public health outcomes. Reducing reliance on fossil fuels will decrease harmful emissions, leading to better air quality and reducing health problems associated with pollution. Additionally, the environmental benefits will include the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.Global knowledge exchange and long-term impact: The creation of the Global Knowledge Platform will facilitate continuous learning, enabling countries to access the latest research, best practices, and technological developments in clean hydrogen. This knowledge-sharing ecosystem will enhance the capacity of countries to innovate and implement hydrogen technologies, while also building a global community of practitioners. The socio-economic benefits of this platform will extend beyond the project’s lifespan, as the lessons learned and products developed will continue to be used by future generations of stakeholders, ensuring sustainable and enduring impacts.The Global Child Project, through its knowledge-driven approach, will not only contribute to the global reduction of CO2 emissions but also bring about lasting socio-economic benefits. By focusing on capacity building, innovation, energy security, and gender inclusion, the project will drive sustainable development in the participating countries and create a transformative model for how clean hydrogen can contribute to industrial growth and social equity.
